# Clinical Metrics

This folder groups the standardized clinical assessment tools and specific patient cohorts used within the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) to evaluate surgical risk and 30-day mortality. It contains direct documentation on the Charlson Score, detailing its role in defining high-comorbidity populations for quality indicators and the data quality issues identified during hospital audits. Additionally, it houses sub-folders that break down specific comorbidity scoring methodologies and track mortality outcomes for distinct patient cohorts stratified by their Charlson Comorbidity Index values.

## Pages

- [[charlson-score|Charlson Score]] — Details the use of the Charlson Score to define high-comorbidity cohorts for quality indicators and highlights data integrity issues identified during regional hospital audits.
- [[topics/clinical-metrics/comorbidity/index|Comorbidity]] — Groups specific clinical indicators used to stratify acute surgery patients by their comorbidity burden, tracking 30-day mortality for cohorts with no registered comorbidities and those with mild to moderate underlying diseases.
- [[topics/clinical-metrics/comorbidity-scoring/index|Comorbidity Scoring]] — Contains documentation on standardized prognostic scales, specifically the Charlson Comorbidity Index, explaining how it stratifies patients by mortality risk and defines cohorts for supplementary quality indicators.
